header: The centring maths of the red badge (NewCircularBadge); I kept it apart so it can be tested without a browser.

symbols.name: inkShift
symbols.sig: export function inkShift(args: { originX: number; baselineY: number; ink: { left: number; right: number; ascent: number; descent: number; weightX?: number }; targetX: number; targetY: number; dpr: number; }): { dx: number; dy: number }

params.name: args
params.type: { originX: number; baselineY: number; ink: { left: number; right: number; ascent: number; descent: number; weightX?: number }; targetX: number; targetY: number; dpr: number; }

doc: How far to move a laid-out text so that its INK is optically centred on (targetX, targetY). originX x where the text starts (its left edge as laid out) baselineY y of its baseline as laid out ink the ink as measured: left/right are distances from the origin (left is positive when the ink reaches LEFT of the origin), ascent/descent are distances above/below the baseline, weightX (optional) is the distance from the origin to the ink's CENTRE OF WEIGHT (positive = right of the origin) dpr device pixels per CSS pixel

Horizontally I use the centre of WEIGHT when it is given, not the middle of the outer edges: a "1" is a heavy stem with a light flag on its left, and the eye takes the stem's side as its centre, so centring its edges leaves it looking too far right. Vertically I use the middle of the digit's height (every digit is equally tall, so its top and bottom margins should match).

Snapping: on a 2x or finer screen every move is snapped to a whole device pixel (crisp, and at most half a device pixel off). On a 1x screen a whole-pixel move is too coarse for the horizontal centre (a "1" may need 0.4px), so I snap it to a quarter pixel instead, which is what text positioning can use; vertically it stays a whole pixel so the digit's top and bottom edges stay sharp.

behaviours: ink 1px LEFT of the target: move it right by 1
ink 1.5px ABOVE the target: move it down by 1.5
ink right of / below the target: negative moves
ink reaching left of the origin and below the baseline: centre = origin + (right-left)/2, baseline + (descent-ascent)/2
with a centre of weight, THAT is what gets centred (weight at 14.2, target 13: move left 1.2), not the edges (which are already centred)
a symmetrical digit (weight at the middle of its edges): no horizontal move
without a centre of weight the middle of the edges is used, as before
2x screen: moves are snapped to half pixels, both ways (0.3 -> 0.5)
1x screen: sideways moves go to a QUARTER pixel (0.4 -> 0.5), up/down moves stay whole pixels (0.3 -> 0)
a move smaller than half a device pixel is no move at all (2x screen)
a narrow '1' and a wide '8' need DIFFERENT horizontal moves
